aimi_behavior_causal_yoyo_title: Yoyo pattern points to execution instability first

aimi_gov_anticipation_decay_blend_max_su: Caps how much HOLD basal/aggressiveness decay is eased toward neutral when prediction relief is high. 0 leaves decay unchanged by anticipation.
aimi_gov_anticipation_hypo_damp_summary: When relief is high, weighted hypo rate for HOLD enter/exit is multiplied by (1 minus this fraction times relief). 0 disables hypo dampening from predictions.
aimi_gov_anticipation_lookback_samples_s: How many recent learning samples (typically 5 min apart) are used to score short-horizon prediction relief. Rounded to a whole number.
aimi_gov_anticipation_margin_mgdl_summar: Minimum predicted BG must be at least hypo threshold plus this margin to count as recovery-oriented for relief.
aimi_gov_hold_agg_decay_rate_summary: Multiplicative decay per update for aggressiveness during HOLD (rate tier).
aimi_gov_hold_agg_decay_severe_summary: Aggressiveness decay per update when severe tier applies.
aimi_gov_hold_agg_floor_rate_summary: Minimum T3C aggressiveness factor during HOLD (rate tier).
aimi_gov_hold_agg_floor_severe_summary: Minimum aggressiveness when severe hypo tier applies.
aimi_gov_hold_basal_decay_rate_summary: Each learning update multiplies basal scaling by this value during HOLD (rate tier). Must be < 1.
aimi_gov_hold_basal_decay_rate_title: HOLD: basal decay per update (rate tier)
aimi_gov_hold_basal_decay_severe_summary: Basal scaling multiplicative decay per update during HOLD when severe tier applies.
aimi_gov_hold_basal_floor_rate_summary: Minimum universal basal scaling factor while HOLD applies without a severe sample in the window.
aimi_gov_hold_basal_floor_severe_summary: Used when at least one sample in the window is at or below the severe hypo BG.
aimi_gov_hypo_bg_mgdl_summary: Post-sample BG below this counts toward hypo rate in the rolling governance window.
aimi_gov_hypo_rate_enter_summary: Fraction of recent samples with BG below the hypo threshold required to enter conservative HOLD (0–1). Lower = harder to trigger.
aimi_gov_hypo_rate_enter_title: Governance: hypo rate to enter HOLD

cal_large_gap_warning: Your blood value (%1$s) is very far from the sensor value (%2$s). One calibration cannot correct a gap this big. A sensor that stays this far off is usually replaced, and the maker normally sends a free replacement. Please talk about it with your care team.
cal_notify_narrow_range: Your calibrations are all close in glucose value, so only a basic correction can be applied. Add one the next time your glucose is clearly higher or lower than usual — spreading calibrations across different levels makes the correction accurate across your whole range, not just around one value.
cal_notify_need_more_entries: Add a fingerstick calibration to activate sensor correction. For the best result: wait until warm-up is over, calibrate while your glucose is steady (not rising or falling fast), and use a fresh, careful meter reading. At least 2 calibrations are needed, ideally at different glucose levels.
cal_notify_stale: It\'s been a while since your last calibration. Sensors can drift over their wear time, so adding a fresh calibration now — while your glucose is steady — helps keep the correction accurate for the rest of the session.
cal_notify_unsafe_fit: Your recent calibrations gave an inconsistent result and are not applied — the sensor is showing uncorrected values. Add a new calibration while your glucose is steady; double-check your meter reading, since a single inaccurate fingerstick can throw this off.
cal_precheck_delta_too_high: Glucose is changing too fast (Δ %1$s %3$s per 5 min, limit %2$s). Wait for stability.
cal_precheck_no_pair: No CGM reading in the last 10 minutes. Check sensor connection.
cal_precheck_warmup: Sensor still in warm-up. Calibration available at %1$s.
cal_reject_delta_too_high: Calibration not saved: BG is changing too fast (Δ %1$s %3$s per 5 min, limit %2$s). Try again when glucose is stable.
cal_reject_no_pair: Calibration not saved: no CGM reading found in the 10 minutes before now.
cal_reject_no_session: Calibration not saved: no sensor session is active. Mark a sensor change first.
cal_reject_warmup: Calibration not saved: sensor is still in the 2-hour warm-up window.
cal_remove_entry_message: This will invalidate the entry. The fit will be recalculated.
cal_saved_need_more_entries: Calibration saved. It will take effect once you add one more fingerstick entry for this sensor (currently %1$d).
cal_saved_unsafe_fit: Calibration saved, but the calculated correction is outside the safe range, so it was not applied. Add another entry, or check your fingerstick value.
cal_sent_to_sensor: Sent to the sensor. It arrives at the next sensor connection, normally within a few minutes. This sensor does not tell the app whether it used the value, so please compare your readings with your meter over the next hour.
cal_status_applied_offset_only: Offset-only calibration applied — sensor range too narrow for slope.
cal_status_applied_slope_clamped: Calibration applied — slope clamped to safe range. Add more entries to relax.

dexcom_oneplus_start_steps:
How to start:
1. Apply the sensor on your body.
2. Paste the applicator Data Matrix (GS1) or enter the 4-digit pairing code — do not wait until after warm-up.
3. Stop Dexcom, xDrip, and Juggluco Direct (only one Bluetooth master).
4. Allow Bluetooth, Scan, select the highlighted sensor, then Connect / follow.
5. Accept the Android Bluetooth pairing prompt if shown.
6. Warm-up ~30 min for a new sensor; attaching to a running sensor can deliver EGVs sooner.

eversense_about_detail:
Setup: enable this source in Config Builder, scan and pair your transmitter, open Status for battery and sync, use Calibration when ready, and Placement if signal is weak.

E365: enter DMS username/password under Credentials for cloud-backed readings.

AIMI: glucose flows into the AIMI loop like any CGM; no extra AIMI preference is required. Physio assistant uses Health Connect separately (not Eversense BLE).

Alarms: sensor/placement/credential issues use unified AAPS notifications (EVERSENSE_* ids). Hypo-risk while looping is handled by AIMI HYPO_RISK_ALARM, not the Eversense driver.

Coexistence / Release: optional modes let the official Eversense app connect periodically.

libre3_presoak_promote_explain:
The pre-soak sensor becomes the sensor that feeds the loop, right away. The sensor you wear now is retired: it stops sending glucose to AAPS and this phone forgets it. This cannot be undone.

You can promote a sensor that is still warming up, for example when the sensor you wear has failed. A warming sensor sends no glucose until its warm-up ends, so the loop has no glucose for that time.

A Libre 3 often reads low and jumpy for about the first half day after it was started. A young sensor can therefore feed the loop readings that do not match your real glucose. Check with a finger stick before you trust it, and talk to your care team if you are not sure what to do.

libre3_presoak_wear_cost: A Libre 3 starts both its warm-up and its 14 day clock at the moment you scan it. There is no way to start a Libre 3 quietly and begin its life later, so a pre-soak spends real wear time: soak it for 12 hours and you have 13.5 days of use left instead of 14.\n\nYou decide when to promote it. There is no smallest soak time.

libre3_start_steps:
How to start:
1. Put the sensor on your arm.
2. Stop the Abbott app and Juggluco. Only one app can hold a sensor.
3. Hold the top of your phone on the sensor until the scan finishes.
4. Allow Bluetooth if you are asked.
5. Warm-up takes about 60 minutes for a new sensor. A sensor that is already running can send glucose sooner.

pref_summary_aimi_advisor_llm_rich_oref: Adds a plain-language facts block for the coach LLM. Turn off for a shorter cloud prompt.
pref_summary_aimi_advisor_personal_oref_: When you open Advisor, trains small models from recent loop+CGM features. Informational only; does not change insulin delivery.
pref_summary_aimi_anticip_basal_floor: When you know you are about to eat, you can tell the loop instead of waiting for it to work the meal out from your glucose going up. Write a note holding the word "anticip" and give it a duration. While that note is open, the loop holds your basal high enough to deliver the amount set below, spread evenly over 30 minutes, and then goes back to normal. No bolus is given and your target is not changed. This is the only setting in AIMI that makes a dose bigger, so it is bounded three ways: the amount you set, the 30 minutes, and the highest rate your pump allows. It stops on its own if your glucose is under 80 mg/dL or is falling by 3 mg/dL or more every 5 minutes, and deleting the note stops it at once. Off by default.
pref_summary_aimi_anticip_meal_evidence: Also let the note above count as proof of a meal inside the loop, so the loop stops waiting for your glucose to confirm one. This is wider than the basal help: meal evidence is one of the things that opens the early release of the dose floor, so it can make the loop dose more in ways the basal help does not. It is a separate switch so the two can be judged apart. Off by default.
pref_summary_aimi_auditor_profile_factor: Lets the AI auditor change the insulin sensitivity (ISF) and the glucose target used by the loop by at most 15 %, up or down, for 15 to 30 minutes. The loop checks every proposal against the last 30 minutes of data and refuses it if one number is wrong. More insulin is never allowed when glucose is under 120 mg/dL, falling, predicted low, after a low, during exercise or with a noisy sensor. The ISF never goes below its usual floor, and all your limits (max SMB, max IOB, max basal, low glucose suspend) still apply. When this is off, the auditor still makes its proposals and writes them to the log, but nothing in your therapy changes.
pref_summary_aimi_autodrive_aggressive_s: On a confirmed aggressive rise, guarantee at least the user-defined Autodrive prebolus amount, delivered as a floor on top of the model SMB. Always re-bounded by Autodrive V3 safety (post-hypo, max SMB, IOB headroom, correction aggression).
pref_summary_aimi_autodrive_v3_authorita: When Autodrive V3 is active and issues a safe SMB/TBR, do not recompute SMB with the legacy MPC/PI blender (prevents post-hypo overshoot). Disable only for debugging.
pref_summary_aimi_basal_channel_safety_g: When a safety rule zeroes the SMB, also block the automatic T3C/Harmonia basal channels instead of letting them take over, and keep the adaptive learner reduction on the rate they propose. Can only lower the automatic temp basal, never raise it. Manual meal modes keep their configured rate.
pref_summary_aimi_basal_projected_error: Size the temp basal on where glucose is heading over the insulin action window, as a single distance from target, instead of adding a separate trend term that outweighed the distance term 36 to 1. Unchanged when glucose is steady; a rise no longer alone drives several times profile basal.
pref_summary_aimi_basal_slew_limit: Limit how fast the basal rate can rise each cycle to smooth out over-corrections. Basal cuts stay instant for hypo safety; meal and forced-boost paths are exempt.
pref_summary_aimi_basal_stack_terminal_c: Uses the same rule on the final basal rate: when the insulin on board could bring glucose under 70 mg/dL by itself, a basal above the profile is brought back to the profile basal. It never goes under the profile basal, and it never acts while a meal is declared. OFF by default: every case is recorded, but the rate is not changed.
pref_summary_aimi_basal_terminal_invaria: Re-check three limits on the temp basal after every multiplier has been applied, instead of before them: hold at profile basal when both glucose and the prediction are below target, while post-hypo recovery is active, or when insulin on board is negative without a rise. Can only lower the rate, never raise it. Manual meal modes are exempt.
pref_summary_aimi_dyn_isf_trajectory_max: Cap on relative ISF adjustment from trajectory (e.g. 0.06 = at most about 6% tighter ISF on a strong rise, or 6% looser on a strong fall). Lower = safer, smaller benefit.
pref_summary_aimi_dyn_isf_trajectory_sha: When on, logs the would-be ISF multiplier but does not change displayed DynISF. Turn off after you trust the signal in logs.
pref_summary_aimi_dyn_isf_trajectory_tun: Uses the same short-horizon CGM features as AutoISF (deltas, parabolic projection, acceleration) only when quality gates pass. Bounded change per tick; skips when physio already tightens ISF strongly. Requires dynamic sensitivity. Off by default.
pref_summary_aimi_dynamic_basal_stack_ca: The dynamic basal can multiply the basal up to 10 times from glucose and trend only. With this on, it does not raise the basal when the insulin on board could bring glucose under 70 mg/dL by itself. It never lowers the basal for that reason, and it never acts while a meal is declared (a meal mode, or a meal note in the last 3 hours). ON by default; every case is recorded.
pref_summary_aimi_effort_activity_protec: Lower SMB when steps and heart rate show current or recent physical effort, even if no activity was declared in AIMI Context. Protection persists for a while after you stop (post-exercise sensitivity) and is skipped when the signals look like stress rather than exercise. Reduction-only.
pref_summary_aimi_engine_hyper_rate_boun: Two rules of the basal engine (slow rise, eventual glucose above 110) have no upper limit and can ask for more than 100 U/h before the max basal cuts them. With this on, they are bound to the profile basal times one glucose factor (0.5 to 5). OFF by default: the bound is recorded, but the rate is not changed.
pref_summary_aimi_forced_tbr_real_pred_d: The early-meal basal for an undeclared meal starts when a rise is detected. With this on, the detector uses the predicted rise instead of the last 5-minute step counted twice, so one noisy reading cannot start it alone. Declared meals are not affected. ON by default.
pref_summary_aimi_high_bg: Glucose level above which AIMI treats the reading as high and switches to its high-glucose dosing paths, such as extra correction and plateau handling. Default 180 mg/dL.
pref_summary_aimi_hrv_baseline_per_night: Your normal HRV is learned from one value per night (the middle reading between 22:00 and 06:00), over the last 7 nights. When this is off, it is learned from the last 28 physio runs, which is only about 7 hours. This changes how a low HRV is judged, and that can change insulin. Off by default.
pref_summary_aimi_hyper_deep_dev: 0 = TDD-scaled default (~120). Deviation above target for DEEP plateau tier.
pref_summary_aimi_hyper_established_dev: 0 = TDD-scaled default (~80). Deviation above target for ESTABLISHED tier.
pref_summary_aimi_hyper_trajectory_relea: When Autodrive V3 is on, lift V3 micro-bolus using scenario projection and trajectory on credible hyper rise. Trigger is not a fixed 200 mg/dL threshold.
Raises HTR SMB floors ~15%% when scenario confirms hyper rise. Use only if default release feels too weak.
pref_summary_aimi_hypo_exposure_guard: Looks at the last 14 days. When more than 4 in 100 readings are below 70 mg/dL (or more than 1 in 100 below 54 mg/dL), extra insulin (SMB, Autodrive, basal boost) is made smaller, and learned settings may only become gentler. Watch only: it writes what it would do in the log and changes no dose.
pref_summary_aimi_max_multiplier: Largest basal rate the adaptive basal feature may use, as a multiple of your profile basal rate. For example, 1.6 means up to 1.6 times your profile basal.
pref_summary_aimi_meal_confirmed_early_r: For undeclared meals: once a meal is confirmed and rising, let the loop reach your configured maximum SMB and basal early, instead of holding back until the high is already established. It only lifts the internal safety floor toward the meal path while blood glucose is climbing, stays within your max SMB, max basal and max IOB, and automatically hands back to the cautious floor once the peak is passed, insulin has stacked, or the rise stops. Real lows and post-hypo protection are never overridden. This raises early dosing, so it is off by default.
pref_summary_aimi_peak_governor_enabled: When adaptive PK/PD is on, blend the insulin profile peak with the learned PKPD peak for loop peakTime (see research doc TAP_G_PEAK_GOVERNOR_RFC).
pref_summary_aimi_peak_governor_learned_: 0 = insulin anchor only, 1 = learned PKPD peak only. Default 0.55.
pref_summary_aimi_pkpd_endo_reversion: Stop the pkpd eventual prediction from sticking at the 39 mg/dL floor once insulin is spent, letting counter-regulation drift it back toward a low-normal. Affects the eventual only; the hypo-protection floor is unchanged.
pref_summary_aimi_pkpd_prediction_kineti: Shape the glucose prediction curves with the adaptive PK/PD learned DIA and peak instead of the fixed insulin profile, so eventual and minPred reflect how your insulin actually acts. Falls back to the profile kinetics when the learner is off or its values are out of range.
pref_summary_aimi_recursive_belief_autho: When on, RBT resolves SMB demand and Traj-Bridge suppression from cross-scale tensions (replaces parallel HTR when release authority is active). Enable only after shadow JSONL review.
pref_summary_aimi_recursive_belief_shado: Build multi-scale belief tree each loop and export recursive_belief (and physiological_patterns when the physio assistant is on) to AIMI_Decisions.jsonl. Required before RBT authority.
pref_summary_aimi_recursive_belief_wavel: Haar 3-band BG decomposition for micro/meso/macro leaves. Off by default.
pref_summary_aimi_rise_ceiling_guard: When glucose climbs fast, the loop can send its biggest allowed bolus again and again, once a minute. Insulin takes 20 to 40 minutes to show, so it can send ten of them before the first one can be seen, and everything sent is still to come once the rise stops. This setting refuses those repeats: after the bolus has come out at its maximum 3 times in a row while glucose is rising by at least 8 mg/dL every 5 minutes, the next ones are held back. The first doses of a rise are never touched, and the temporary basal rate is not changed. Off by default. This switch changes your doses: when it is on, boluses are really held back during a fast rise, and you may run higher after a meal. When it is off, nothing is held back; the verdict is only written to the exported data, so you can measure what it would have done before you turn it on.
pref_summary_aimi_sensor_confidence_cgm_: Base sensor confidence on the CGM source and signal, not on wearable/health data availability. The old formula let a missing watch collapse sensor confidence and block Harmonia/RBT all day even with a good CGM. When on, a native/filtered CGM is trusted and an unknown source stays cautious rather than fully blocking. This raises dosing authority, so it is off by default.
pref_summary_aimi_smb_training_min_quali: Rows with a quality value below this limit are not used to train the SMB model. A lower limit gives more rows, but rougher data. A higher limit gives cleaner data, but fewer rows. Standard: 0.40. Changing it starts a new training at the next loop run.
pref_summary_aimi_smb_training_relaxed_f: On: rows that only have the harmless dual delivery flag (SMB and temp basal in the same loop run) are kept, and check rows are taken from every period. Off: the old filter, any flag removes the row, so the model may get almost no SMB rows.
pref_summary_aimi_sos_enable: Send SMS with BG, trend, IOB and location when a severe hypo or missing CGM data is detected. SMS only (no automatic calls).
pref_summary_aimi_sos_immediate_threshol: BG (mg/dL) that triggers an immediate SOS SMS (also triggered when delta ≤ −10 mg/dL).
pref_summary_aimi_sos_phone: Primary phone number for SOS SMS (include country code, e.g. +33…).
pref_summary_aimi_sos_phone2: Optional second contact. Identical numbers are deduplicated so only one SMS is sent.
pref_summary_aimi_sos_stale_threshold: If no valid CGM reading is seen for this many minutes, send a missing-data SOS SMS.
pref_summary_aimi_sos_threshold: BG (mg/dL) below which the 30-minute observation window starts. Recovery requires returning above this value + 10.
pref_summary_aimi_straight_line_tube: Discrete short-horizon control on max SMB: keeps predicted minimum BG above a floor using the PKPD min curve, favors larger caps when eventual BG is high, penalizes zig-zag SMB sizing. Does not replace PKPD or safety nets. Off by default.
pref_summary_aimi_stress_isf_floor: When you are under stress, keep the insulin sensitivity used by the loop at or above your profile value, instead of letting it drift below. Stress is detected only from the watch: heart rate at least 20 bpm above your resting rate, fewer than 250 steps in the last 15 minutes, and both held without a break for at least 10 minutes. Once it is on, it stays on until the signs have been gone for 5 minutes, so a few steps do not turn it off and on again. It works at any hour of the day or night. When it is on, it can only make doses smaller, never larger, because a higher sensitivity means the loop expects more from the insulin already active. When it is off, the same check still runs and is written to the log, but nothing in your therapy changes. If the heart rate or the resting heart rate is missing, the floor stays off.
pref_summary_aimi_t3c_autodrive_basal_au: Under T3C brittle mode, fuse Autodrive’s temporary basal demand with the T3C PI controller. SMB from Autodrive is never delivered (basal-only). The physiological tree can unlock a higher basal ceiling and faster ramp on a confirmed rise. Off disables fusion (PI-only + shadow Autodrive).
pref_summary_aimi_t3c_cfrd_cob_delay: Minutes to shift the COB prediction curve forward for delayed/irregular carbohydrate absorption. Feeds basal anticipation only (no SMB). Range 0–90 min.
pref_summary_aimi_t3c_cfrd_exacerbation: Manual flag for active pulmonary exacerbation or corticosteroid treatment. Raises the T3C basal aggressiveness ceiling while CFRD mode is on. Turn off when the exacerbation ends. Off by default.
pref_summary_aimi_t3c_cfrd_lgs_floor: Minimum LGS threshold (mg/dL) used by T3C anticipation when CFRD mode is on. Impaired counter-regulation needs a higher floor than typical T1D. Range 70–95.
pref_summary_aimi_t3c_cfrd_mode: Cystic fibrosis–related diabetes adaptations under T3C: higher LGS safety floor, delayed COB absorption for malabsorption, and inflammation-aware basal aggressiveness. Basal-only (no SMB). On by default when T3C brittle mode is used. This is not medical advice — review with your CF/diabetes care team.
pref_summary_aimi_t3c_hyper_basal_floor: Under T3C brittle mode, when glucose has stayed at or above 160 mg/dL for at least 20 minutes, hold the basal at your configured Max basal rate so sensor noise cannot collapse the correction to zero. Basal only (no SMB). Releases automatically once glucose falls back below 160 mg/dL. On by default. This is not medical advice — review your settings with your care team.
pref_summary_aimi_tpo_enabled: Temporarily lowers correction aggression for 45 min after post-hypo, poor sleep, or hyper→hypo exhaustion. Requires Control Center autonomy ≥ Assisted application. Reverts automatically.
pref_summary_aimi_tpo_llm_confirm_enable: When on, AIMI applies a TPO session only if the advisor LLM confirms the clinical context (uses the same API keys as AI Coach). When off, algorithm triggers apply directly.
pref_summary_aimi_tpo_notify_on_apply: Shows a system notification when a 45 min protection session starts or ends. Tap to open OpenAPS AIMI preferences.
pref_summary_aimi_traj_bridge_basal_surv: When the trajectory safety bridge asks for a lower temp basal, apply that request again after the basal schedule has run, so the schedule can no longer write over it. Can only lower the rate, never raise it, and does nothing on a loop run where the bridge did not ask for anything. Off by default; the request is recorded either way.
pref_summary_aimi_tree_meal_rise_frontlo: On a corroborated meal rise (tree = NEED_MORE_INSULIN, BG above target, rising), let Harmonia apply the early SMB lift even when sensor confidence is low — instead of waiting for established hyper. Only ever softens the authority (never a hard bolus); real hypo, free-fall and safety blocks are never overridden. Off by default: it overrides the sensor-confidence gate. Fix the sensor source first if you can.
pref_summary_aimi_tube_hyper_clamp_physi: Above 160 mg/dL the prediction is held at 80 mg/dL, whatever insulin is on board. With this on, the dose check uses instead the glucose that the insulin on board would reach by itself. With little insulin on board, a rising glucose can get more SMB. With a lot of insulin on board, the SMB is blocked. ON by default; every case is recorded so it can be reviewed.
pref_summary_aimi_tube_veto_ignore_floor: The dose feasibility check refuses every bolus when the predicted lowest glucose sits under the hypo floor. That prediction cannot go below 39 mg/dL, so a curve that reached its own limit looks like a coming low. With this on, the bolus limit is released only while glucose is high and flat, never during exercise, never after a low and never while glucose is falling. This is the only setting here that can raise a dose. Off by default; the case is recorded either way, so you can count how often it happens first.
pref_summary_aimi_undeclared_cob: Estimates virtual carbs from the glucose appearance rate (Ra), BG dynamics, patient weight/TDD and rest/activity context, then feeds them into the prediction curves so basal (TBR) anticipates an undeclared meal. Never delivers autonomous SMB. Automatically muted during exercise, hypo/post-hypo, pulmonary exacerbation and any stress/dawn false-meal suppression. Off by default.
pref_summary_aimi_undeclared_cob_max_g: Upper bound (grams) for the virtual carbs the estimator may inject into the prediction path. Lower = safer and smaller effect. Only used when undeclared-meal COB estimation is on.
pref_summary_alert_hyper: Notify when glucose is at or above the high threshold.
pref_summary_alert_hypo: Sound an alarm when glucose is at or below the low threshold.
pref_summary_alert_override_dnd: When enabled, AAPS alarms play through silent and Do Not Disturb modes (alarm stream). When disabled, alarms respect silent/DND (notification stream).
pref_summary_alert_rapid_fall: Sound an alarm when glucose drops by at least the configured amount within the configured time window.
pref_summary_alert_sound: The AAPS sound, or a softer melody if loud sounds are hard for you. If a melody cannot be played, the AAPS sound is used.
pref_summary_aps_always_use_short_deltas: Always use short average delta instead of simple delta for BG change calculations.
pref_summary_aps_autosens_adjust_targets: Allow Autosens to adjust target glucose in addition to basal and ISF.
pref_summary_aps_dynisf_adjust_sensitivi: Adjust sensitivity calculations when using DynamicISF.
pref_summary_aps_high_tt_raises_sensitiv: High temporary targets will increase insulin sensitivity.
pref_summary_aps_low_tt_lowers_sensitivi: Low temporary targets will decrease insulin sensitivity.
pref_summary_aps_resistance_lowers_targe: When resistance is detected, lower the target glucose.
pref_summary_aps_sensitivity_raises_targ: When sensitivity is detected, raise the target glucose.
pref_summary_aps_smb_on_even_target: Alternative activation of SMB always based on target glucose value.
pref_summary_aps_use_dynamic_sensitivity: Use DynamicISF for sensitivity adjustment instead of Autosens.

scene_wizard_careportal_info: A CarePortal event is a log entry — it does not change insulin delivery or algorithm behavior. Use it to mark activities, situations, or notes in your treatment timeline. You can review these records in Treatments - CarePortal and in Nightscout, helping you and your doctor spot patterns in your data.
scene_wizard_chain_info: Optionally chain another scene to auto-activate when this one expires. You can also skip to it when ending early. The follow-up runs only if the target is enabled and the pump is available; otherwise you will get a notification.
scene_wizard_choose_template: Pick a starting point. Templates pre-fill recommended actions for common situations — you can adjust everything in the following steps.
scene_wizard_driving_desc: Slightly higher target to stay safe behind the wheel.
scene_wizard_duration_info: Duration controls how long this scene stays active. When time runs out, duration-based actions (temporary target, profile switch, running mode) expire on their own, while persistent changes (like the SMB toggle) are automatically reverted to their previous values. Setting duration to 0 makes the scene indefinite — all actions stay active until you end the scene manually.
scene_wizard_exercise_desc: Raise target, reduce profile to 70%, disable SMB to prevent exercise lows.
scene_wizard_hot_weather_desc: Reduced profile — heat accelerates insulin absorption.
scene_wizard_info_alcohol: Alcohol is one of the most dangerous situations for people with type 1 diabetes. The liver prioritizes processing alcohol over releasing glucose, which can cause delayed hypoglycemia 6–24 hours later — often overnight while you are asleep. LGS mode prevents insulin stacking by only reducing delivery when glucose drops. A reduced profile and disabled SMB further limit insulin on board. Always check your blood glucose before going to sleep and consider setting an alarm for a middle-of-the-night check.
scene_wizard_info_bathing: When you disconnect your pump, insulin delivery stops completely — no basal, no boluses, no corrections. The algorithm switches to disconnected mode and stops making adjustments. This is normal for short periods like showering, bathing, or swimming. When the scene ends, the pump reconnects and the algorithm resumes automatically. Keep disconnects short — without basal insulin, blood glucose will start rising within 1–2 hours.
scene_wizard_info_driving: Safe driving requires stable blood glucose above 5.0 mmol/L (90 mg/dL). In some countries, checking before and during long drives is a legal requirement. A slightly higher target gives the algorithm a safety buffer — it will work to keep you above the level where concentration and reaction time start to decline. If you go low while driving, pull over immediately, treat the hypo, and wait at least 45 minutes after glucose returns to normal before continuing.
scene_wizard_info_exercise: During physical activity, muscles consume glucose faster and insulin sensitivity increases. Raising your temporary target beforehand gives the algorithm a head start — it will begin reducing insulin delivery early, building a buffer against exercise-induced lows. Disabling SMB is also recommended, since correction boluses during exercise can cause rapid drops. For best results, activate this scene 1–2 hours before you start exercising so the algorithm has time to lower your insulin on board.
scene_wizard_info_hot_weather: High temperatures cause blood vessels to dilate, which accelerates insulin absorption — the same dose hits faster and harder. This can lead to unexpected lows, especially during outdoor activities. A modest profile reduction (85%) compensates for the faster absorption. Stay hydrated, monitor more frequently, and be aware that insulin stored in a warm pump or pen may degrade. If you are also exercising in the heat, consider combining this with the exercise scene for additional protection.
scene_wizard_info_luteal_phase: Many women experience increased insulin resistance during the luteal phase (roughly 1–2 weeks before their period). This is caused by rising progesterone levels that reduce insulin sensitivity. The effect varies enormously between individuals — some notice a 10–30% increase in insulin needs, others see minimal change. Start with a conservative increase (115%) and adjust based on your own patterns over several cycles. Tracking this in CarePortal helps identify your personal rhythm.
scene_wizard_info_medical_procedure: During surgery or medical procedures, anesthesia and stress hormones make blood glucose unpredictable. Open loop mode is recommended because the algorithm cannot reliably predict what your body will do under these conditions. A higher target (150 mg/dL) provides a safety margin against intraoperative hypoglycemia. Disabling SMB prevents unexpected insulin delivery during the procedure. Always inform medical staff that you are wearing an insulin pump and CGM. For procedures longer than 3 hours, your team may switch to intravenous insulin instead.
scene_wizard_info_post_exercise_night: After physical activity, muscles keep refilling glycogen stores for many hours — insulin sensitivity can stay elevated for 24–48h, with the highest risk of nocturnal hypoglycemia 6–12h after exercise. A reduced profile lowers basal delivery throughout the night, a higher temporary target gives the algorithm a safety buffer, and disabling SMB prevents the algorithm from over-correcting brief rises. Activate this scene at bedtime on days you exercised, especially after longer sessions or when you added new activities. Keep fast carbs at the bedside and consider setting an alarm for a middle-of-the-night check.
scene_wizard_info_pre_meal: Setting a lower target 30–60 minutes before eating tells the algorithm to start building up insulin on board before carbs arrive. This helps blunt the post-meal spike that happens when food hits the bloodstream faster than insulin can act. Best used when you know a meal is coming soon.
scene_wizard_info_sick_day: Illness, fever, and stress hormones can dramatically increase insulin resistance — sometimes by 50% or more. A stronger profile (e.g. 150%) tells the algorithm to deliver more insulin across all calculations — basal rates, bolus suggestions, and correction factors. You can also add a temporary target or adjust the running mode in the following steps. Monitor closely and adjust as your body recovers.
scene_wizard_info_sick_day_vomiting: When you cannot keep food down, the standard sick day approach of increasing insulin can be dangerous. Vomiting means carbs are not being absorbed, so blood glucose may drop rather than rise. A reduced profile (60%) lowers insulin delivery, and LGS mode adds an extra safety net by suspending insulin if glucose falls. Disabling SMB prevents any extra boluses. Monitor frequently — check blood glucose every 1–2 hours and ketones every 2–4 hours. Seek medical help if vomiting persists more than a few hours or ketones rise above 1.5 mmol/L.
scene_wizard_info_sleep: Overnight is when many people experience undetected highs or lows. A slightly tighter target during sleep lets the algorithm make finer corrections throughout the night. Pair this with a profile that reflects your nighttime basal needs for best results.
scene_wizard_loop_mode_info: The running mode determines how much autonomy the algorithm has. In Closed Loop, it adjusts insulin delivery automatically. LGS (Low Glucose Suspend) only reduces or stops insulin when glucose is falling toward a low — it will not increase delivery. Open Loop calculates suggestions but waits for you to confirm each one.

scene_wizard_medical_procedure_desc: Open loop with SMB off for surgery or medical procedures.
scene_wizard_name_info: Choose a name and icon that make this scene easy to recognize at a glance. You will see these on the activation button and in the active scene banner on your overview screen.
scene_wizard_post_exercise_night_desc: Reduced profile, higher target, SMB off — protects against delayed overnight lows after activity.
scene_wizard_pre_meal_desc: Lower target to get ahead of the post-meal spike.
scene_wizard_profile_info: A profile switch changes your basal rates, insulin sensitivity factor (ISF), and insulin-to-carb ratios (IC) all at once. You can scale everything by percentage — for example, 110% increases basal delivery, bolus calculations, and carb absorption rates by 10%. You can also switch to a different profile entirely if you have one set up for specific situations.
scene_wizard_sick_day_desc: Stronger profile (150%) to handle increased insulin resistance during illness.
scene_wizard_sick_day_vomiting_desc: Reduced profile with LGS — opposite of standard sick day when you cannot absorb food.
scene_wizard_sleep_desc: Tighter target for better overnight control.
scene_wizard_smb_info: Super Micro Boluses (SMB) let the algorithm deliver insulin upfront as small boluses while temporarily stopping basal delivery to compensate — effectively borrowing insulin from the future for a faster response. Disabling SMB prevents this and limits the algorithm to adjusting basal rates only. The response becomes slower and more gradual, which is often preferred during exercise or sleep.
scene_wizard_tt_info: A temporary target tells the algorithm to aim for a different blood glucose level for a set period. With a higher target, the algorithm reacts more slowly to rising glucose and targets a higher value overall — this reduces insulin delivery and helps prevent lows during exercise. With a lower target, the algorithm responds sooner and delivers more insulin — useful for getting ahead of a meal. Pick one of your presets below — the target value and reason are already configured there.
